 From the Songkran celebrations in April to key royal and religious observances, employees can look forward to several periods of break, with additional bank closures applying to selected institutions.
 Thailand's 2027 public holiday calendar features a range of national celebrations, religious observances and commemorative occasions throughout the year. These include the traditional Songkran Festival in April, Chinese New Year in February and several royal anniversaries. 
 The calendar also features holidays such as National Children's Day, Teachers' Day and the Royal Ploughing Ceremony Day. Separately, the Bank of Thailand (BOT)   has outlined 18 holidays for financial institutions and specialised financial institutions (SFIs), alongside additional arrangements for selected institutions and branches. 
 Full list of Thailand's 2027 public holidays 
 The following dates are listed in chronological order, based on the 27 holidays featured in GovtHolidays ' curation. 
 January 
 1 January (Friday): New Year's Day
 2 January (Saturday): New Year Special Holiday
 10 January (Sunday): National Children's Day
 16 January (Saturday): Teachers' Day 
 February 
 6 February (Saturday): Chinese New Year's Day
 7 February (Sunday): Second Day of Chinese New Year
 8 February (Monday): Third Day of Chinese New Year 
 March 
 3 March (Wednesday): Makha Bucha Day 
 April 
 6 April (Tuesday): Chakri Day
 13 April (Tuesday): Songkran Festival
 14 April (Wednesday): Songkran Holiday 
 May 
 1 May (Saturday): National Labour Day
 4 May (Tuesday): Coronation Day
 13 May (Thursday): Royal Ploughing Ceremony Day
 31 May (Monday): Visakha Bucha Day 
 June 
 1 June (Tuesday): Substitute holiday for Visakha Bucha Day
 3 June (Thursday): Birthday of H.M. Queen Suthida Bajrasudhabimalalakshana 
 July 
 28 July (Wednesday): Birthday of H.M. King Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
 29 July (Thursday): Asarnha Bucha Day 
 August 
 12 August (Thursday): Birthday of H.M. Queen Sirikit the Queen Mother 
 September 
 24 September (Friday): Mahidol Day 
 October 
 13 October (Wednesday): Anniversary of the Death of H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great 
 23 October (Saturday): Chulalongkorn Day 
 December 
 5 December (Sunday): Birthday of H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great
 6 December (Monday): Observed holiday for H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great's Birthday
 10 December (Friday): Constitution Day
 25 December (Saturday): Christmas Day 
 Additional holidays for financial institutions in Thailand 
 BOT has published a separate calendar of 18 holidays for financial institutions and SFIs in 2027. 
 While several dates overlap with the wider public holiday calendar, the banking schedule includes substitute holidays for observances that fall on weekends. 
 The 18 banking holidays are: 
 1 January (Friday): New Year's Day
 22 February (Monday): Substitute holiday for Makha Bucha Day
 6 April (Tuesday): Chakri Memorial Day
 13 April (Tuesday): Songkran Festival
 14 April (Wednesday): Songkran Festival
 15 April (Thursday): Songkran Festival
 3 May (Monday): Substitute holiday for National Labour Day
 4 May (Tuesday): Coronation Day
 20 May (Thursday): Visakha Bucha Day
 3 June (Thursday): Birthday of H.M. Queen Suthida Bajrasudhabimalalakshana
 19 July (Monday): Substitute holiday for Asarnha Bucha Day
 28 July (Wednesday): Birthday of H.M. King Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
 12 August (Thursday): Birthday of H.M. Queen Sirikit the Queen Mother and National Mother's Day
 13 October (Wednesday): H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great Memorial Day
 25 October (Monday): Substitute holiday for H.M. King Chulalongkorn the Great Memorial Day
 6 December (Monday): Substitute holiday for H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great's Birthday, National Day and Father's Day
 10 December (Friday): Constitution Day
 31 December (Friday): New Year's Eve 
 Additional arrangements for selected banks and branches 
 Beyond the 18 nationwide banking holidays, the BOT has outlined additional arrangements for certain financial institutions and branches. 
 For the Islamic Bank of Thailand , additional holidays will be observed for: 
 Eid al-Fitr (Hari Raya Puasa)
 Eid al-Adha (Hari Raya Haji) 
 The dates will follow announcements by the Sheikhul Islam Office . These additional holidays will apply only if they do not fall on any of the existing holidays or on a Saturday or Sunday. 
 Meanwhile, branches of financial institutions and SFIs in five southern provinces will also observe additional holidays for the following occasions: 
 Eid al-Fitr
 Eid al-Adha
 Chinese New Year 
 The five provinces are Narathiwat , Pattani , Yala , Satun and Songkhla . These additional closures are also subject to the dates not coinciding with existing holidays or weekends. 
 The BOT has also confirmed that two previously observed banking holidays remain discontinued. These are the mid-year closing holiday on 1 July, which was cancelled from 2019 onwards, and the additional annual account-closing holiday on 1 April for the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives , which was cancelled from 2022 onwards. 
 The changes reflect improvements in financial institutions' accounting systems, which allow them to manage financial statements without disrupting services across their operating channels. 
 Planning ahead for 2027 
 Employers and employees can use the 2027 holiday calendars to plan annual leave, workforce arrangements and business operations ahead of time. Organisations should also take note of the separate banking holidays, particularly if they have employees or business activities in southern Thailand, and check for further official announcements before finalising their plans.
